_doc: BALROG / MiniHack testbed config for the shared meta-harness (AutoSpatial/harness_map). The benchmark repo at ~/workspace/BALROG is NEVER modified: evaluator.py injects a HarnessAgentFactory into BALROG's own EvaluatorManager, which takes the factory as an argument.
_rubric_doc: The OFFICIAL BALROG 8, in config.yaml order. Now that the search set AND the holdout are both the official 8 (user decision 2026-09-12), one fixed label list serves both - which it could not when the evolve split was a different task set. fitness.vector maps score.json's per_task_vector onto these, so the per-eval checkpoint records per-task detail instead of an empty per_instance.

fitness._primary_doc: TRUE post-rollout success: end_status == TASK_SUCCESSFUL, read from the env's own terminal flag. NOT BALROG's `progression`, which tests `reward >= 1.0` (progress.py:165) and therefore scores a genuine solve as a failure whenever the final step's reward is 1.0 minus the step penalty (0.99). MEASURED on the anchor: 1 of 10 successes lost across 57 episodes, and a whole task misclassified (Corridor-R2 solved 3/3, progression reported 67%). BALROG's unmodified progression is still emitted and carried in dense[] for leaderboard comparability.

_noise_doc: With adapt.sigma = 0 there is no hand-set noise floor, so the MEASURED per-field SE is the only way to read a split against its own noise. A binary metric has SE ~ sqrt(p(1-p)/n): ~0.27 at n=3, ~0.22 at n=5, ~0.15 at n=10.
_adapt_doc: sigma 0 = project default (see harness-map defaults). thr = 2*sigma gates ZOOM-IN (split if cell_range > 2s), ZOOM-OUT (revert unless a descendant beats pre-split elite by 2s) and cell_signature bucketing. At 0 every distinct fitness is its own bucket — the b->0 limit the engine documents as maximally shape-sensitive. 0.02 / 0.05 are ablation arms only.

meta_agent._doc: Proposer / judge / diagnostician backbone. cli:claude = shell out to the Claude Code CLI with the GENERAL harness_map skills. Pinned explicitly: MetaAgent.backbone defaults to chat-loop (hosted, needs OPENAI_API_KEY), so omitting this block would silently select the hosted path. Overridable at runtime via META_BACKBONE.

audit._privileged_doc: The oracle surface for MiniHack. A harness sees obs['text'] (the language wrapper's rendering) and its own trajectory. Reaching past that into env internals, the .des level definition, the goal coordinates, or the terminal success flag is a cheat. end_status/progression are listed because a harness that reads its own success flag mid-episode could trivially game the score.
audit._judge_file_doc: run_judge writes `<genome_dir>/judge.json` (meta_agent/agent.py:610). Declaring judge_verdict.json here made config.audit_from_dir read MISSING on every candidate even when the judge had produced a real verdict — the verdict reached Fitness.judge in memory but never the on-disk audit trail the selection key and the finalizer read.

balrog._doc: Where the benchmark lives and how the frozen agent backbone is reached. The repo is read-only from this testbed's point of view.

_valid_doc: Explicitly 'rows' rather than 'auto'. NOTE the reason is NOT that an all-zero vector is falsey - a dict of zeros is truthy, so auto/bool(vector) would admit a candidate scoring 0 on all 8 tasks correctly. 'rows' is chosen because the vector is only as good as score.json carrying per_task_vector: if that key is ever absent (an older score file, a partial run), vector collapses to {} and 'auto' would silently mark every candidate INVALID. Validity should track 'did episodes actually run', which is exactly bool(rows).
_anchor_doc: harnesses/naive = BALROG's published naive agent, behaviourally unchanged, in the rich-harness skeleton (measured 2.5% +/- 2.47% on the official 8, n=40; faithfulness audited 2026-09-13 — 21 claimed divergences, 20 refuted under 3-vote adversarial verification, and the one survivor was an adapter out_dir bug, not a harness divergence). It is the ONLY anchor. A hand-built harness previously existed as a human-expert comparator and was DELETED 2026-09-13; its measured numbers are archived in balrog_baselines/REFERENCE_POINTS.json.
